result.note: Tests the March 2026 easing of FDI rules for land-bordering countries and the timeline of the India–China thaw.

questions.prompt: In March 2026, India changed its rules on foreign direct investment from land-bordering countries. Consider the following statements about the change:
items: Investments where Chinese beneficial ownership stays below 10% now enter through the automatic route.
Proposals in electronics, batteries, rare-earth magnets, capital goods and solar cells will receive a government decision within 60 days, provided Indian residents retain majority control.
The relaxation applies only to investments from China and not to other land-bordering neighbours.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 3 is wrong because the change is part of a broader policy covering all land-bordering neighbours, though it is squarely aimed at rebuilding commercial ties with Beijing. Under the previous policy, any firm with a Chinese beneficial owner needed government approval regardless of stake, which caught global PE and VC funds with Chinese limited partners.
questions.source: Now, investments where Chinese beneficial ownership stays below 10% enter through the automatic route.

questions.prompt: Consider the following pairs relating to the thaw in India–China commercial ties:
items: Narendra Modi's first visit to Beijing in seven years — August 2025
Clearance of business visas for Chinese technicians — February 2026
questions.ask: How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.explain: Business visas for Chinese technicians were cleared in December 2025; February 2026 was when state-run power and coal companies were allowed to resume equipment imports. The visa freeze had stalled projects such as Bengaluru's Yellow Line metro for years.
questions.source: business visas for Chinese technicians were cleared in December
